newsitem.title: India: India shares end off lows, Bajaj Auto rises.
newsitem.headline: India shares end off lows, Bajaj Auto rises.

text.p: Share prices across Indian bourses recovered from an early plunge on Thursday to finish modestly lower, traders said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 9.20 points, or 0.29 percent, lower at 3,163.78, after sliding to 3,122.76.
Scooter maker Bajaj Auto unveiled a 27 percent rise in its net profit to 2.26 billion rupees in the six-month 1996/97 (April-March) against 1.77 billion in the year-ago period.
Bajaj share rallied 14.75 rupees, or 1.56 percent, to 956.25 at the BSE.
After trading ended steel giant Tata Iron & Steel Company (TISCO) and tractor maker Mahindra & Mahindra released better results for the first six months to September 30, 1996.
TISCO said its net profit rose 25 percent to 2.52 billion rupees after providing for 373.5 million for new minimum tax.
"It's beyond our expectations," said Anurag Mathur, steel analyst at Peregrine Capital. "There's been an improvement in operating margins."
A trader said the results were better than expectations but was unlikely to spur a rally. TISCO rose to 186/187 rupees in the kerb after it lost 5.50 rupees to 181.25 on the BSE.
M&M said its net rose 25 percent to 924.3 million rupees from 738.10 million. Its share rose 2.50 rupees to 315.

ITC finished 1.0 rupee higher at 304 after falling 11 rupees to 292 in early deals, following Wednesday's 18.25 rupees loss after a government agency arrested top company officials for alleged foreign exchange violations.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index fell 17.07 points to close at 909.29.
SBI rose 0.25 rupees to 230.50 and ACC 22.50 to 1,529.25 while Reliance lost 3.0 at 202.50.
